text:
oliver: quick RFC follow-up — proposing SLO-aware page-pinning policy for streaming inference to avoid p99 spikes when KV-cache misses show up. sketch attached, tl;dr: pin only when expected latency benefit outweighs mem cost and tenant budget allows.

raj: can you summarize the scoring function and the major knobs?

oliver: short: score = (expected_delta_p99 * w_latency) - (mem_cost_bytes * w_mem). if score > threshold && tenant_budget_token available => pin. expected_delta_p99 estimated from hotness + historical miss penalty.

michelle: how do we get expected_delta_p99 cheaply at runtime? offline models, or a running estimator?

oliver: light estimator in runtime: keep per-model prefix counters + EWMA of miss penalty (resident_latency vs nonresident_latency). we only sample a small fraction of requests to update stats. conservative defaults for cold models.

kevin: i'm worried about fragmentation: long-lived pins can bloat VRAM and increase compaction pressure. what's the mitigation?

oliver: pins are leasem and soft-preemptable. we have three classes: transient (per-request, auto-release), session (short TTL ~60s), anchored (explicit API). background compactor treats pinned regions differently: low-score pinned ranges are candidates for preemptive eviction with callbacks to recompute caches.

jessica: multi-tenant fairness: could a noisy tenant game the system to pin everything?

raj: plan is per-tenant token-bucket budget (refill rate + burst). admission enforces budget; plus tenant_weight included when aggregating score so heavy tenants have diminishing returns.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: runtime v0.42.3 queued — includes experimental metrics and flags: slo_pin_enabled, pin_budget_ratio, pin_ttl_default.

michelle: other edge: quantized models with shared KV pages across layers. pin one page benefits many requests. do we account for shared benefit?

oliver: yes, score aggregates expected QPS * per-request delta_latency across active workloads that reference the page. shared pages get higher score automatically; estimator uses reference counts and sampled request distributions. estimator conservative to avoid overpinning.

kevin: please add a simulation harness before rollout. we need to validate p99 improvement vs memory fragmentation and compaction overhead. synthetic long-tail prompt workloads + trace replay.

oliver: agreed. plan: 1) implement estimator + policy flags in canary pool, 2) run 24h simulation with production traces (evict-sim), 3) collect metrics: p99 delta, pin_count, fragmentation metric, compaction run-time.

jessica: SGTM. small note: make flags per-deployment (hosted/dedicated/private); default OFF for private installs.

raj: observability: expose per-tenant metrics: pin_count, pin_hits, evict_reasons, estimated_delta_p99, token_bucket_tokens. add trace logs when an eviction preempts a pinned range.

michelle: can you paste the minimal config we'll use for the canary?

oliver: sure — snippet below. will put full RFC in doc repo and link in the review invite.

oliver: ```yaml
slo_pin:
  enabled: true
  pin_budget_ratio: 0.15
  pin_ttl_secs: 60
  score_weights:
    latency: 1.0
    memory: 0.5
  tenant_token_bucket:
    refill_qps: 1000
    burst: 2000
```

kevin: :thumbsup: can you schedule a short design review tomorrow (30m)?

oliver: booked — will post agenda + links to sim and the draft RFC. thanks all!
